question.question: Which progress responsibility applies when a full leader and a metadata-only witness commit an entry, the other full voter lacks that entry, and the leader becomes unreachable: is majority availability owed to the connected full-voter/witness pair or restricted by an explicit witness fault contract?

feedback.answered: Additional contract investigation found that docs/devops.md promises availability with quorum and recommends observer catch-up/promotion for replacement. It also distinguishes permanent quorum loss, for which ImportSnapshot is an operator tool. ImportSnapshot documentation explicitly says not to use it while a majority remains running or failures are temporary, requires stopped NodeHost and an exported snapshot, and its membership validator rejects converting an existing witness to a regular node. Thus this operator tool is not an automatic survivor continuation for the currently investigated majority-connected interval, and it cannot simply promote metadata into missing payload. Node entry guards also reject witness proposals, reads and transfer requests. These sources strengthen the practical question but still do not give an explicit witness-specific applicability rule for generic availability language; the vote-freshness safety protection remains valid. No new execution was performed or reinterpreted. Separately, the in-memory state-machine adapter and NativeSM.Update forward the Result value without copying Data, completing the inspected producer-to-cache return chain. A caller mutation permission or output-buffer reuse duty is still not established; no second defect is claimed.
